title: Databases
subtitle: One-click managed databases with a persistent volume.
name: Name
deleteConfirm: Delete this database and its volume? All data is lost. This cannot be undone.
keepVolume: Keep the data volume (don't delete the data)
dangerDeleteDesc: Permanently remove this database and (optionally) its data volume. This cannot be undone.
connectionPending: Connection details appear once the database is deployed.
empty: Spin up Postgres, MySQL, Redis and more in one click.
stopConfirm: Stop this database? Apps that depend on it will lose their connection until it is started again.
cloneHint: Creates a new, un-deployed database with the same engine and settings. Data and backups are not copied.
cloneWarn_data_not_copied: Clone created — its configuration was copied, but no data. Deploy it to start fresh.
cloneWarn_host_port_reset: The external port was cleared on the clone to avoid a conflict — set a new one if you need external access.
envDesc: Extra variables injected into the database container. The engine's own credential variables are managed and cannot be overridden.
envRedeploy: Deploy the database to apply the new variables.
volumesDesc: Extra named volumes mounted into the database container (beyond the managed data volume). Data survives redeploys.
volumesRedeploy: Deploy the database to mount the new volumes.
moveServerDesc: Move this database to another server in the team. Only possible before the first deploy.
moveServerLocked: Already deployed — its data lives on the current server and can't be moved. Back it up and restore to a new database on the target server instead.
moveServerDone: Moved. Deploy it on the new server when ready.
iconHint: A square PNG (32–512px). Overrides the engine logo across the panel.
iconTooLarge: That image is too large even after cropping — pick a smaller one.
connectionDesc: Apps on the same server reach this database by its internal host. Keep the credentials secret.
publicConnectionDesc: Reachable from outside Tugra — point GUI tools or other hosts here. Same credentials.
publicPortNoIp: A public port (:{port}) is mapped, but this server has no known public address yet — set its public IP under Servers to get an external connection URI.
backupsDesc: Dumps are written to the server's disk. Restoring overwrites the current data.
verifyLatestHint: Restore the latest backup into a disposable throwaway database to prove it actually restores, then tear it down.
verifyFailedToast: Backup did not restore — check restore history
restoreConfirm: Restore this backup? It overwrites the current database.
restoreToConfirm: Pick a compatible database (same engine). This overwrites the target's data.
backupCronHint: A 5-field cron (e.g. 0 3 * * * = 03:00 daily). When set it overrides the hours interval.
backupRetentionDaysHint: Also delete backups older than this many days (blank = no age limit). The newest backup is always kept.
exportHint: Generate a temporary download link for this S3 backup to import it on another server.
exportExpiry: Link expires in 24 hours — paste it into "Import from URL" on the target database.
exportFailed: Could not generate a migration URL.
importDesc: Restore an external dump (curl'd by the agent) into this database — overwrites current data.
importConfirm: This overwrites the database with the imported dump. Continue?
backupUnsupported: Backups for this engine aren't available yet.
limitsDesc: Optional CPU/memory limits and a container health check. Applied on next deploy.
healthCmd: Health check command (e.g. pg_isready -U tugra || exit 1)
publicPortDesc: Expose this database on a host port so external clients can connect. Leave empty for internal-only access.
publicPortInternal: Currently internal-only (reachable by apps on the same network).
provisioningCardBody: Pulling the image and starting the container. Connection details will appear here in a moment.
runNoReason: No error output was recorded for this run.
runReasonHidden: The failure output is only visible to members who can manage backups.
runDownloadFailed: Could not generate a download link
runLocalNote: This backup is stored on the server's local disk. Add an S3 destination to download backups from here.
verifyScheduleHint: Periodically restore the latest backup into a disposable database to prove it still restores, then tear it down. Independent of the backup schedule.
verifyCronHint: A 5-field cron (e.g. 0 4 * * 0 = 04:00 every Sunday). When set it overrides the hours interval. Keep it sparse — each run provisions a real database.
verifyScheduleFailed: Could not save the verify schedule
pitrDesc: Continuously archive WAL to the backup destination so this database can be restored to any moment, not just to a backup. Postgres only.
pitrEnableConfirm: Enabling PITR restarts this database once (a few seconds of downtime) and then verifies that WAL archiving works. If verification fails, archiving is turned back off automatically. Continue?
pitrDisableConfirm: Disabling PITR ships any remaining WAL to the destination, then restarts the database without archiving. Continue?
pitrPurgeSpool: Discard WAL that cannot be shipped
pitrPurgeSpoolHint: If some archived WAL cannot be uploaded to the destination, delete it anyway. The recovery window for that period is lost.
pitrNeedsBase: No base backup since PITR was enabled. WAL alone cannot anchor a recovery — take one now.
pitrLocalWarning: The backup destination is this server's local disk, so archived WAL offers no protection against losing the server. Point backups at S3 for real disaster recovery.
pitrArmingHint: Archiving was switched on but not yet verified (the hub may have restarted mid-way). Finish enabling to verify it, or disable to roll back — either restarts the database.
pitrResumeConfirm: This restarts the database and re-verifies WAL archiving. If verification fails, archiving is turned back off automatically. Continue?
pitrDisablePurgeConfirm: Disabling PITR ships any remaining WAL to the destination and restarts the database without archiving. You chose to DISCARD any WAL that cannot be shipped — the recovery window for that period will be lost. Continue?
pitrStatusUnavailable: PITR status could not be loaded — retrying.
pitrBaseFailed: Base backup failed — see the base backups list for details
